evidence_class: agent-drafted candidates; UNREVIEWED; not a dataset
status: review queue - every judgement below is a PROPOSAL, not ground truth
notes: 35 candidate development queries drafted on 2026-09-17 to top up the CodeRank development qualification from the 29 conformant rows cobra-v2.json supplies to 64. Do not merge into a dataset before a human has annotated the spans and cleared the review notes. Companion: coderank-qualification-candidate-queries.md.

source_of_truth.source_method_used: git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/spf13/cobra into the session scratchpad, then git checkout a0a6ae020bb3899ff0276067863e50523f897370
source_of_truth.source_method_not_used: Go module cache: the Go module cache reported by `go env GOMODCACHE` contains no github.com/spf13 directory at all, so there was nothing to read there.
source_of_truth.checkout_head_subject: Improve API to get flag completion function (#2063)

span_convention: Line numbers follow cobra-v2.json exactly: a span starts at the first line of the declaration's doc comment (or at the declaration itself when there is none) and ends at the closing brace in column 0. The convention was reverse-engineered from cobra-v2.json and verified to reproduce cb-01, cb-02, cb-22, cb-24, cb-33, cb-11, cb-15, cb-18 and cb-23 byte-for-byte before any candidate was written. Sub-spans (a few lines inside a larger function) follow the precedent of ci-43, ci-1111 and ci-1289.
id_convention: cq-NN, following the <prefix>-<number> convention of cb-NN (cobra-v1 rows) and ci-NNNN (issue-derived rows). 'cq' = cobra qualification. Chosen so the ids collide neither with cb-01..cb-40 (cb-05 withdrawn but reserved), nor with ci-*, nor with the cd-* ids used by docs/eval/retrieval/drafts/2026-09-14-holdout-shaped-dev/dataset.json.
family_convention: cobra-family-<first 16 hex of sha256('coderank-qualification:' + key)>, the same shape and derivation style as docs/eval/retrieval/drafts/2026-09-14-holdout-shaped-dev/generate.py. All 35 are distinct from each other and were checked against all 224 cobra-family-* ids occurring anywhere in this repository (cobra-v2.json included), not just cobra-v2.json.
shortfalls: None. All 35 requested candidates were produced and every one has at least one grade-3 span that was read at the pinned revision.

grade3_span_collisions_with_cobra_v2.method: Computed, not estimated: every grade-3 span below is byte-identical to a grade-3 span already used by a cobra-v2.json row. Partial overlaps (a function inside a whole-file exact_path span, or a sub-span inside a larger function) are NOT listed here; they are pervasive and are inherent to the exact_path stratum.
grade3_span_collisions_with_cobra_v2.reviewer_decision_required: Whether a new family may reuse an existing family's grade-3 span. cobra-v2.json already does this internally (command.go:1146-1168 is the grade-3 span of five distinct families), so the precedent permits it; the qualification's own rule governs.

what_is_not_verified: Grades. Every grade is a proposal. The grade-3/grade-2 boundary in particular is a judgement call the reviewer owns.

Family collisions by meaning. Family *ids* are provably unique; whether a candidate belongs to an existing family by topic or paraphrase is a human call. Every case I could see is listed in candidates_with_review_notes.
Answer-span token budgets. Some grade-3 spans are large (bash_completionsV2.go:31-379 is 349 lines) and may not fit whatever ceiling the qualification applies.
Whether the qualification's conformance rules accept whole-file exact_path spans, sub-spans, or struct-field spans.
